answer: A reef mooring bond blocks cloned agents. Each identity moors one lotus raft to a reef post with a vine line, locks 70 credits, and pays a fee: first 36, k-th 36+7(k-1), and 1,000 fakes pay 3,532,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. An auditor recomputes vine sag from the reef current table for the lotus load; a claim over the table by more than 5 percent, or a reused reef post serial, burns the bond and voids the identity. A rented-raft ring fails because one reef post cannot moor two lotus rafts under different keys. An honest agent pays 36 once and recovers its bond after a clean check.
